children.name: Fluctuation in Cycles
children.hovertext: Menstrual cycles become irregular-shorter, longer, or skipped, as hormone levels fluctuate during this phase.

children.name: PMS Worsening
children.hovertext: PMS Worsening during Menstrual Cycle

children.name: Cramps
children.hovertext: Cramps during Menstrual Cycle

children.name: Stress
children.hovertext: Stress may feel stronger, harder to recover from, and can amplify other symptoms.

children.name: Anxiety
children.hovertext: Fluctuation in estrogen levels can lead to Anxiety

children.name: Mood Swing
children.hovertext: Fluctuation in testosterone and estrogen can lead to Mood Swings

children.name: ADHD
children.hovertext: Changes in estrogen during perimenopause can disrupt dopamine regulation, which may worsen ADHD symptoms such as inattention, overwhelm, and emotional reactivity.

children.name: Panic
children.hovertext: Panic attacks may become more frequent or intense due to hormonal changes.

children.name: Anger
children.hovertext: Small frustrations can trigger sudden irritability or outbursts due to hormonal fluctuations.

children.name: Depression
children.hovertext: Depressive symptoms varied by ethnicity in SWAN study, with sharp increases over time among Japanese and Hispanic women, and associations with higher testosterone levels

children.name: Weight Gain
children.hovertext: Weight gain may occur more easily, especially around the abdomen, even without changes in diet or activity. Hormonal shifts can affect metabolism, fat storage, and insulin sensitivity. Unexplained weight gain is one of the early indicators of Perimenopause.

children.name: Body Odour
children.hovertext: Body odor may change or become stronger. Hormonal shifts can increase sweating and alter skin bacteria, leading to noticeable changes in scent.

children.name: Bone Health
children.hovertext: Bone density may begin to decline as estrogen and testosterone levels fluctuate, increasing the risk of bone loss over time.

children.name: Breast Tenderness / Pain
children.hovertext: Breast Tenderness are often caused by fluctuations in Progesterone levels. It is one of the early indicators of this stage.

children.name: Body Aches
children.hovertext: Body aches like Muscle & joint pain

children.name: Frozen Shoulder
children.hovertext: Shoulder stiffness and pain may increase due to hormonal changes.

children.name: Tinnitus
children.hovertext: Tinnitus or Ringing Ear are one of the least discussed symptoms. It may appear or worsen during perimenopause. Hormonal changes can affect the inner ear and nervous system, leading to ringing or buzzing sounds.

children.name: Electric Shock Experience / Tremors
children.hovertext: Sudden electric shock-like sensations or internal tremors may occur. These can feel brief but intense and are linked to nervous system sensitivity during hormonal fluctuations.

children.name: Insulin Resistance
children.hovertext: Insulin resistance may increase during perimenopause. Hormonal changes can affect how the body processes sugar, making blood glucose harder to regulate.

children.name: Dry Mouth
children.hovertext: Dry mouth may occur as hormonal changes affect saliva production, leading to discomfort or a persistent dry sensation.

children.name: Insomnia
children.hovertext: Sleep disruption affects ~38% of women and often co-occurs with hot flashes. Rates vary by race/ethnicity ~ lowest (28%) observed in Japanese and highest (40%) in Caucasian women. Symptoms are also associated with estrogen volatility and low progesterone.

children.name: Fatigue
children.hovertext: Fatigue may feel persistent or overwhelming, even with adequate rest. Hormonal changes can disrupt sleep, energy regulation, and recovery.

children.name: Vivid Dreams
children.hovertext: Dreams may become more vivid, intense, or memorable. Hormonal changes can affect sleep cycles and REM sleep, making dreams feel more lifelike.

children.name: Brain Fog
children.hovertext: Brain fog may cause forgetfulness, slower thinking, or difficulty concentrating. Reduced Estrogen levels and Hormonal fluctuations can affect memory, attention, and mental clarity.

children.name: Migraine
children.hovertext: Migraine/ Headache often caused due to low or absent Progesterone. It is one of the early indicators of Perimenopause.

children.name: Memory Lapse
children.hovertext: Decline in Progesterone could lead to Memory Lapse.

children.name: Dizzy / Vertigo
children.hovertext: Dizziness or vertigo may occur, causing a spinning sensation or feeling unsteady. Hormonal fluctuations can affect balance, blood flow, and the inner ear.

children.name: Decreased Attention
children.hovertext: Decreased attention often due to fluctuating testosterone & estrogen

children.name: Hot Flashes & Night Sweat
children.hovertext: Sudden waves of heat, flushing, or sweating may occur during the day or night. Hot flashes affect up to 70% of women, vary by race/ethnicity ~ Rates are high among African-American & Native American women ; Chinese & Japanese women have lower rates & a shorter overall duratiion of hot flashes. Elevated FSH and fluctuating estrogen are predictive of hot flashes.

children.name: Heart Palpitations
children.hovertext: Fluctuation in Estrogen levels could lead to heart palpitations or irregular heart beat.

children.name: Low/High Libido
children.hovertext: Libido may increase or decrease during perimenopause. Hormonal fluctuations can affect desire, arousal, energy levels, and comfort. Fluctuations in testosterone and progesterone can lead to decreased Libido

children.name: Frequent Urination
children.hovertext: Declining estrogen can weaken pelvic tissues and increase bladder sensitivity, leading to frequent urination.

children.name: Urinary Tract Infection
children.hovertext: Urinary tract infections may occur more often during perimenopause. Hormonal changes can affect the urinary tract lining and natural protective bacteria.

children.name: Vaginal Dryness & Irritation
children.hovertext: Vaginal symptoms are common during perimenopause and are associated with declining estrogen levels. 60% of Central American women reported vaginal dryness compared with 21% of non-Hispanic Caucasian women

children.name: Painful Intercourse
children.hovertext: Decreased Estrogen levels often lead to pain or discomfort during intercourse

children.name: Hair Thinning or Loss
children.hovertext: Hair may become thinner or shed more than usual. Hormonal changes can affect hair growth cycles, leading to noticeable thinning over time.

children.name: Skin Issues
children.hovertext: Acne may appear or worsen during perimenopause. Hormonal shifts can increase oil production and inflammation, leading to breakouts even if acne wasn’t an issue before.

children.name: Allergy
children.hovertext: Allergies may appear or worsen during perimenopause. Hormonal changes can affect immune responses, making the body more sensitive to triggers.

children.name: Dry & Itchy Ear
children.hovertext: Ears may feel dry or itchy as hormonal changes affect skin moisture and sensitivity.

children.name: Dry Skin
children.hovertext: Skin may become drier, itchier, or more sensitive. Hormonal changes can affect collagen, oil production, and skin barrier function.

children.name: Brittle Nail
children.hovertext: Nails may become brittle, thin, or prone to breaking as hormonal changes affect keratin production and moisture.
